title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 6.2 Obligations of Children to Parents

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

After the command to worship Allah alone, the Qur'an commands kindness to parents. In this sub-strand you will outline what children owe their parents, study the guidance in Qur'an 17:23-24, and practise obedience and respect in daily life.

## Strand 6.0: Muamalaat (Social Relations)
Sub-strand 6.2: Obligations of Children to Parents
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) outline obligations of children to their parents
b) assess the importance of obeying and respecting parents as a religious obligation
c) demonstrate ways to obey and respect parents
d) appreciate their parents by respecting and obeying them

## Key inquiry questions
1. How do you show obedience and respect to your parents?
2. Why should children be dutiful towards their parent?

## Core competencies
• Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively is enhanced as learners describe the duties of children to their parents, in groups, and present in class.
• Citizenship: the skill of social and cultural sensitivity and awareness is enhanced as learners dramatise children’s obligations to their parents.
• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners dramatise children’s obligations to their parents.

## Values
• Respect enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinion while discussing the importance of obeying and respecting their parents.
• Responsibility enhanced as learners dramatise children’s obligations to their parents.
• Love enhanced as learners listen to qasidas/anashid (e.g. Ummy) on the importance of respecting and obeying parents from a digital device.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Responsibility by relating well with parents and other members of the society.

## Links to other learning areas
• Social Studies: as learners fulfil their duties and responsibility towards parents and other members of the society.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 6.0 Muamalaat (Social Relations), Sub-strand 6.2 Obligations of Children to Parents
• Qur'an 17:23-24
• Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: the deeds most loved by Allah include prayer at its time and kindness to parents

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Duties of children towards their parents

LESSON 1: DUTIES OF CHILDREN TOWARDS THEIR PARENTS
==================================================

## What you will learn
• Outline the obligations of children to their parents.
• Give a daily example of each duty.

Curriculum outcomes: a) outline obligations of children to their parents

## Introduction
Your parents have names, needs and feelings. Islam does not leave a child's behaviour towards them to chance. It sets clear duties.

## Notes
### Birr al-walidayn
Birr al-walidayn means being dutiful to parents. It is one of the greatest good deeds in Islam. The duties below are ways a Grade 4 learner lives that teaching.

### What children owe their parents
- Obedience in what is right: do what they ask when it does not involve disobeying Allah. If a parent ever asked a child to lie, steal or skip a duty to Allah, the child would not do that wrong act, but would still speak kindly.
- Respectful speech: answer when they call, and do not shout, mock or interrupt.
- Help: wash dishes, sweep, carry a light item, look after a younger sibling, or run a safe errand.
- Learning: attend school and madrasa, do homework, and practise what they have taught of the deen.
- Care: bring water when they are tired, sit with them when they are unwell, and not add to their worry.
- Dua: ask Allah to have mercy on them and to reward them.
- Honesty: tell them the truth about where you go and who you are with.
- Permission: ask before leaving the house or using something that belongs to them.

### Small acts count
Dutifulness is not only for the day a parent is old. It starts now, in the tone you use at breakfast and in the way you respond when you are asked to put away your books. A child who waits to be begged to help has not yet understood the duty. A child who offers help has begun to fulfil it.

These duties are owed to both mother and father. Where a child is raised by a guardian, the same respect and help are due to the person who carries the parent's role.

## Key words
• birr al-walidayn — being dutiful and good to one's parents
• obedience — doing what a rightful authority asks
• guardian — a person who brings up a child in place of a parent

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Mother asks Aisha to take the younger child to the tap and wait with him. Aisha's friend wants her to come and play at once. What is Aisha's duty?

Working:
1. Helping a parent and caring for a sibling is an obligation.
2. Play can wait until the task is done.

Answer: Aisha should obey her mother, take the child safely, and play later.

## Activity: Our duties to our parents
You will need: Exercise book
1. In groups, discuss the duties of children to their parents.
2. List at least six duties and write them in your notebook.
3. Beside each duty, write one example from a school day or a day at home.
4. Present the list in class and listen to the other groups.

## Practice
1. What does birr al-walidayn mean?
2. List four obligations of children to their parents.
3. What should a child do if asked to do something Allah has forbidden?
4. Give one way a learner can help at home today.

## Summary
• Children owe parents obedience in what is right, respect, help, honesty and dua.
• These duties are called birr al-walidayn.
• They are practised in small daily actions, not only in old age.

### Answers to practice
1. Being dutiful and good to one's parents.
2. Any four: obey them in what is right, speak respectfully, help at home, study, care for them, make dua, be honest, ask permission.
3. Not do that wrong act, but still speak kindly to the parent.
4. Any one: wash dishes, sweep, look after a younger sibling, arrange books, or run a safe errand.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Qur'an 17:23-24 and why obedience matters

LESSON 2: QUR'AN 17:23-24 AND WHY OBEDIENCE MATTERS
===================================================

## What you will learn
• State the teachings of Qur'an 17:23-24 about parents.
• Explain why obeying and respecting parents is a religious obligation.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the importance of obeying and respecting parents as a religious obligation

## Introduction
Some commands in the Qur'an stand next to the command to worship Allah alone. Kindness to parents is one of them. That placement shows how serious the duty is.

## Notes
### The meaning of Qur'an 17:23-24
Allah says, in meaning: Your Lord has commanded that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to your parents. If one or both of them reach old age while they are with you, do not say to them a word of disrespect, and do not scold them, but speak to them with noble words. Lower yourself before them in mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.

### What the verses teach
- Worship of Allah comes first. Dutifulness to parents comes immediately after that command.
- The Arabic sound "uff" is a small grunt of annoyance. The verse forbids even that. If a tiny sound of irritation is forbidden, shouting, insulting and rolling the eyes are more clearly wrong.
- Speak noble words: "Yes, Mother," "Thank you, Father," and a gentle answer when you are corrected.
- Lower the wing of humility: be soft, not proud, especially when parents are old, weak or slow.
- Make dua for mercy on them, remembering that they cared for you when you could do nothing for yourself.

### Why this is a religious obligation
- It is Allah's command, not only a custom of the community.
- The Prophet (S.A.W) was asked which deed Allah loves most. He said the prayer at its time. Asked what was next, he said kindness to parents (Bukhari and Muslim).
- Parents gave years of care before the child could repay anything. The verses tell us to remember that care.
- A home where children obey and respect parents is peaceful. The child also learns how to treat other people.
- Disrespect hurts the parents and displeases Allah. Respect pleases both.

Obedience here is part of worship. A learner who lowers the voice at home is practising the Qur'an, not only avoiding punishment.

## Key words
• uff — a small sound of annoyance that the Qur'an forbids saying to parents
• noble word — speech that is kind, polite and honourable
• humility — being gentle and not proud

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Grandmother, who is caring for Yusuf as his parent does, asks him to repeat a message because she did not hear. He says "uff" and walks away. Which part of Qur'an 17:23 has he broken, and what should he say instead?

Working:
1. The verse forbids even the word of annoyance, uff.
2. He should speak a noble word and repeat the message kindly.

Answer: He should not say uff. He should turn back, repeat the message gently, and speak with respect.

## Activity: The verse in our notebooks
You will need: A copy or chart of the meaning of Qur'an 17:23-24, Exercise book
1. Read the meaning of Qur'an 17:23-24 aloud in groups.
2. Discuss why obeying and respecting parents is a religious obligation.
3. Write four points from the discussion in your notebook, including the command not to say uff and the dua for parents.
4. Share one point with the class and listen respectfully to others.

## Practice
1. Which command comes immediately after worshipping Allah alone in Qur'an 17:23?
2. What does the verse say about the word uff?
3. Write the meaning of the dua in Qur'an 17:24.
4. After prayer at its proper time, which deed did the Prophet (S.A.W) mention as most loved by Allah?

## Summary
• Qur'an 17:23-24 joins kindness to parents with the worship of Allah alone.
• Even a sound of annoyance is forbidden; speech must be noble and humble.
• Children ask Allah to have mercy on their parents.

### Answers to practice
1. To be kind to parents.
2. Do not say a word of disrespect or annoyance, such as uff, to parents.
3. My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.
4. Kindness to parents.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Showing obedience and respect every day

LESSON 3: SHOWING OBEDIENCE AND RESPECT EVERY DAY
=================================================

## What you will learn
• Demonstrate ways of obeying and respecting parents.
• Choose personal actions that show appreciation.

Curriculum outcomes: c) demonstrate ways to obey and respect parents; d) appreciate their parents by respecting and obeying them

## Introduction
Respect is easy to talk about and harder to do when you are tired, corrected, or in a hurry to play. The Sunnah is lived in those ordinary moments.

## Notes
### Ways to obey and respect
- Answer at the first call, not the fifth.
- Use a low, polite voice. Do not argue in public or embarrass them.
- Do the chore you were given, and do it fully.
- Put shoes straight, clear your sleeping place, and keep your clothes where you were told.
- Tell them when you reach school and when you leave, if that is the family rule.
- When they advise you, listen to the end before you reply.
- If you make a mistake, say sorry without excuses that blame them.
- Pray for them after swalah: "Rabbir hamhuma kama rabbayani sagheera" — My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.
- When they are old or sick, give them the comfortable seat, help them walk, and do not hurry them.

### Appreciation
Appreciation means you notice their effort and you show it. You can thank them for a meal, tell them you love them, and avoid comparing them unkindly with other families. Songs and qasidas such as Ummy, which praise the mother, remind the heart of this love. Listening is useful only if the behaviour at home changes.

### A scene to avoid
A learner who obeys the teacher but shouts at home has not understood birr. Parents come before friends. If friends laugh at a child for helping at home, the child can say calmly that helping parents is part of faith, and then continue the task.

Practise one new act of respect this week and keep it. Small repeated acts build a dutiful character.

## Key words
• qasida — a poem or song, here an Islamic poem about parents
• Ummy — an Arabic word for my mother; also the name of a well-known nashid about the mother
• appreciation — noticing a person's goodness and showing that you value it

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Father is speaking to a visitor. Omar interrupts to ask for money for a game. How can Omar show respect instead?

Working:
1. Interrupting is poor manners.
2. He should wait, greet the visitor, and ask quietly when the talk has paused, or wait until the visitor leaves.

Answer: He should wait and speak politely at the right time, instead of interrupting.

## Activity: Drama and a nashid
You will need: Space for a short play, A digital device to listen to a qasida or nashid such as Ummy, if available
1. In groups, dramatise two scenes: a child obeying a parent cheerfully, and a child speaking rudely, then correcting the behaviour.
2. The class names the respectful actions they saw.
3. Listen to a short qasida or nashid about parents and write one lesson from it.
4. Each learner writes two ways he or she will obey and respect parents this week.

## Practice
1. Give three ways of showing respect to parents at home.
2. What is the meaning of 'Rabbir hamhuma kama rabbayani sagheera'?
3. Why is it not enough to respect the teacher but shout at home?

## Summary
• Respect is shown by a quick answer, a gentle voice, finished chores and honest apology.
• The dua of Qur'an 17:24 is said for parents.
• Appreciation is proved by behaviour, not only by songs and words.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: answer when called, use a polite voice, do chores fully, do not interrupt, apologise when wrong, make dua for them, help them when tired.
2. My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.
3. Dutifulness to parents is a religious duty and comes before pleasing friends.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 6.2 OBLIGATIONS OF CHILDREN TO PARENTS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Birr al-walidayn means…
   A. being dutiful to parents
   B. skipping school
   C. travelling alone
   D. arguing to win

2. Which of these is a duty of a child?
   A. Shouting when called
   B. Helping with housework
   C. Leaving without permission
   D. Hiding the truth

3. A child is asked by a parent to cheat in an exam. What should the child do?
   A. cheat to show obedience
   B. refuse the wrong act and still speak kindly
   C. insult the parent
   D. cheat and then laugh

4. In Qur'an 17:23, kindness to parents is placed just after which command?
   A. the rules of trade
   B. the command to worship Allah alone
   C. the story of Taif
   D. the rules of farming

5. Why does the Qur'an forbid saying uff to parents?

6. The dua in Qur'an 17:24 asks Allah to…
   A. make the child rich at once
   B. have mercy on the parents as they raised the child
   C. punish the neighbours
   D. cancel swalah

7. Which deed did the Prophet (S.A.W) place next after prayer at its time?
   A. Kindness to parents
   B. Collecting pictures
   C. Sleeping late
   D. Arguing

8. Which action demonstrates respect?
   A. Interrupting a parent who is speaking
   B. Waiting and then speaking politely
   C. Rolling the eyes
   D. Walking away while they are talking

9. Give two ways a learner can show appreciation to parents this week.

10. A nashid such as Ummy is useful when…
   A. it is listened to and then ignored at home
   B. it reminds the heart and the learner's behaviour becomes more respectful
   C. it replaces obedience
   D. it is used to mock parents
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 6.2 OBLIGATIONS OF CHILDREN TO PARENTS
========================================

1. A. being dutiful to parents
   It is the Islamic name for goodness and duty towards parents.

2. B. Helping with housework
   Help, honesty, permission and respectful speech are all part of the child's obligations.

3. B. refuse the wrong act and still speak kindly
   Obedience is in what is right. A wrong command is not obeyed, but kindness remains.

4. B. the command to worship Allah alone
   The verse joins tawhid with kindness to parents, which shows the weight of the duty.

5. Even a small word of annoyance is disrespect. Children must speak to parents with noble words.
   If uff is forbidden, harsher speech is also forbidden.

6. B. have mercy on the parents as they raised the child
   The child remembers being small and cared for, and asks mercy for the parents.

7. A. Kindness to parents
   This Hadith shows that birr is among the deeds Allah loves most.

8. B. Waiting and then speaking politely
   Noble speech and patience are part of Qur'an 17:23.

9. Any two: thank them, make dua, do a chore without being pushed, speak gently, listen to advice.
   Appreciation is shown in actions as well as words.

10. B. it reminds the heart and the learner's behaviour becomes more respectful
   Songs about parents support the duty; they do not replace it.

## Practice
1. Give three ways of showing respect to parents at home.
2. What is the meaning of 'Rabbir hamhuma kama rabbayani sagheera'?
3. Why is it not enough to respect the teacher but shout at home?

## Summary
• Respect is shown by a quick answer, a gentle voice, finished chores and honest apology.
• The dua of Qur'an 17:24 is said for parents.
• Appreciation is proved by behaviour, not only by songs and words.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: answer when called, use a polite voice, do chores fully, do not interrupt, apologise when wrong, make dua for them, help them when tired.
2. My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.
3. Dutifulness to parents is a religious duty and comes before pleasing friends.

questions.question: Birr al-walidayn means…
questions.explanation: It is the Islamic name for goodness and duty towards parents.

questions.question: Which of these is a duty of a child?
questions.explanation: Help, honesty, permission and respectful speech are all part of the child's obligations.

questions.question: A child is asked by a parent to cheat in an exam. What should the child do?
options: refuse the wrong act and still speak kindly
questions.explanation: Obedience is in what is right. A wrong command is not obeyed, but kindness remains.

questions.question: In Qur'an 17:23, kindness to parents is placed just after which command?
options: the command to worship Allah alone
questions.explanation: The verse joins tawhid with kindness to parents, which shows the weight of the duty.

questions.question: Why does the Qur'an forbid saying uff to parents?
questions.answer: Even a small word of annoyance is disrespect. Children must speak to parents with noble words.
questions.explanation: If uff is forbidden, harsher speech is also forbidden.

questions.question: The dua in Qur'an 17:24 asks Allah to…
options: make the child rich at once
have mercy on the parents as they raised the child
questions.explanation: The child remembers being small and cared for, and asks mercy for the parents.

questions.question: Which deed did the Prophet (S.A.W) place next after prayer at its time?
questions.explanation: This Hadith shows that birr is among the deeds Allah loves most.

questions.question: Which action demonstrates respect?
options: Interrupting a parent who is speaking
Walking away while they are talking
questions.explanation: Noble speech and patience are part of Qur'an 17:23.

questions.question: Give two ways a learner can show appreciation to parents this week.
questions.answer: Any two: thank them, make dua, do a chore without being pushed, speak gently, listen to advice.
questions.explanation: Appreciation is shown in actions as well as words.

questions.question: A nashid such as Ummy is useful when…
options: it is listened to and then ignored at home
it reminds the heart and the learner's behaviour becomes more respectful
it is used to mock parents
questions.explanation: Songs about parents support the duty; they do not replace it.
